title: Machine learning nominates a postpartum microRNA associated with later diabetes
summary: LASSO-based screening nominated plasma microRNAs in women with previous gestational diabetes. In a separate 82-person sample set from the same longitudinal cohort, miR-369-3p remained associated with later type 2 diabetes after adjustment and multiple-testing correction. Adding it to clinical factors raised apparent AUC from 0.83 to 0.92, with overlapping confidence intervals. The final prediction model was evaluated after marker selection in that sample; prospective clinical utility remains untested.
ai_technology: LASSO logistic regression; bootstrap feature selection
organization: Western Sydney University; University of Sydney; University of Melbourne

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Twenty-one-person discovery screening and separate 82-person biomarker measurements within a 103-woman longitudinal cohort.
evidence.unknown: Independent-cohort replication, causal microRNA function and frozen-model prospective prediction remain unestablished; final-model performance can be optimistic.
evidence.ai_role: L1-penalized logistic regression and repeated bootstrap selection prioritize microRNAs for subsequent measurement and outcome-association analysis.
